thread:
kelsey: heads-up — hitting a weird hang in the Python SDK async client on Windows when the environment uses a custom CA bundle and CERTIFI is effectively bypassed. quick repro and notes below.

devin: can you paste minimal repro + which python versions you tried?

kelsey: repro steps: create venv, `pip install redwood-sdk certifi==2023.11.1`, then point SSL_CERT_FILE to a concatenated bundle that includes a corp CA. run this script: 
```py
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def main():
    client = AsyncClient(api_key="sk-TEST")
    r = await client.chat.create(model="gpt-mini", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}])
    print(r)

asyncio.run(main())
```
On my machine (Windows 10, venv, pip) it just never returns — process stays running, CPU low, no exception.

ben: interesting. what python versions? 3.8/3.11/3.12? also is this in WSL or native windows?

kelsey: native windows. tested on 3.8.16 and 3.12.0. 3.12 works fine, 3.8 hangs. i also tried with REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and SSL_CERT_FILE unset vs set; behavior changes. with standard certifi bundle it works.

maria: could be the default ProactorEventLoop on recent windows python causing underlying openssl/socket interplay to hang when custom cert set. try forcing selector event loop policy: 
```py
import asyncio
import sys
if sys.platform == "win32":
    asyncio.set_event_loop_policy(asyncio.WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy())
```
That fixed a similar hang for me in another client.

kelsey: confirmed — forcing selector policy makes the repro complete on 3.8. thanks! 😅

devin: nice catch. did you get any SSL error logs when it hung, or was it silent?

kelsey: basically silent. i put a logging hook around socket.recv and saw it block at the SSL handshake read call. no python exception.

ben: sounds like event loop + openssl blocking issue. we should add a troubleshooting note in the Windows section of the SDK quickstart about event loop policies and cert bundle precedence. also add an FAQ entry about env vars REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE vs SSL_CERT_FILE and certifi precedence.

kelsey: small SDK bug/feature request: AsyncClient doesn't implement __aenter__/__aexit__ for async context manager so folks try `async with AsyncClient(...) as c:` and get a typing/error mismatch. it'd be great to either add the methods or document explicit `await client.close()` pattern. mypy flagged it too.

jordan: please open a GH issue with repro + minimal script + env dump (pip freeze, windows build info). tag it 'windows', 'async', 'certs', '3.8'. i'll pick it up.

kelsey: filed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/2543 with repro + logs + resolution note (switching loop policy).

ci-bot: created issue #2543 and linked PR template.

devin: followups: 1) add quickstart blurb, 2) add test matrix run on windows 3.8 with custom CA bundles in CI (maybe as an opt-in job), 3) consider adding async context manager for AsyncClient to satisfy typing + cleanup ergonomics.

ben: +1 to all three. also add a short snippet in the Windows troubleshooting page showing the `asyncio.set_event_loop_policy(...)` workaround.

kelsey: thanks team — saved me a ton of time. leaving notes in our internal quickstart doc too. :thumbsup:
